title: Delta-Map Belief Updates for Stable Spatial Revision in Vision-Language Models

contributions.purpose: Enable VLMs to maintain and revise spatial beliefs over time without wasteful and error-prone full cognitive-map regeneration.
contributions.mechanism: A delta-map belief update interface that treats cognitive maps (structured JSON) as external state and updates them through sparse delta operations with explicit preserve/overwrite rules.
contributions.evaluation: On the Theory of Space benchmark, providing prior map context improves false-belief identification F1 by +16.7 percentage points over scratch regeneration.
contributions.source_quote: First, we propose a delta-map belief update interface for VLMs that treats cognitive maps as external state and updates them through sparse delta operations.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate that prior map context matters for detecting environmental changes.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical comparison of update conditions with vs. without prior map context on the Theory of Space benchmark.
contributions.evaluation: Prior context improves change detection by +54% relative improvement (false-belief identification F1 +16.7 points).
contributions.source_quote: Second, we provide empirical validation on the Theory of Space benchmark demonstrating that prior context dramatically improves change detection (+54% relative improvement).

contributions.purpose: Show that sparse targeted updates are as accurate as full regeneration while being more efficient.
contributions.mechanism: Comparison of delta-map sparse updates against full map regeneration, plus analysis of per-step object update rates.
contributions.evaluation: Sparse updates match full regeneration (F1 = 0.479 vs 0.477) with 52-63% smaller structured outputs; only ~30% of objects require updating per step.
contributions.domain: efficient spatial memory for embodied AI
contributions.source_quote: Third, we present evidence that sparse updates match full regeneration performance with substantial efficiency gains, validating the sparse evidence premise for spatial belief revision.

self_declared_provenance.quote: These works focus primarily on spatial extraction from static scenes, whereas our work addresses the distinct challenge of spatial belief revision over time.
Our work builds on the cognitive map representation from Theory of Space but focuses specifically on how to efficiently update these representations when environments change.
Our delta-map approach contributes to this literature by proposing sparse, targeted belief updates that preserve unchanged information while selectively revising only affected elements

notes: Explicit three-contribution list at end of Introduction (spans pages 1-2). C3 reports an equivalence/tie result (F1 0.479 vs 0.477) framed positively as efficiency gain.
